name: Colwood

facts.text: Removing a protected tree in Colwood needs a Tree Management Permit under Urban Forest Bylaw No. 1735.
facts.excerpt: If the tree you are planning to remove is a protected tree, you will need to obtain a Tree Management Permit.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: Colwood's Urban Forest Bylaw rack card treats trees 30 cm (12 in) in diameter or more as protected; significantly altering one also needs a permit.
facts.sourceTitle: Urban Forest Bylaw rack card (City of Colwood)
facts.excerpt: If you would like to remove or significantly alter a protected tree you will need a permit.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Smaller species-specific thresholds (Garry oak, arbutus etc.) in research/areas.json were not re-confirmed this session.

facts.text: A Colwood tree permit application needs a Tree Site Plan or Tree Management Plan plus photos; removing more than five protected trees needs a Tree Management Plan by a qualified professional.
facts.sourceUrl: https://www.colwood.ca/sites/default/files/trees/2017 October 4 Tree Management Permit Application City of Colwood.pdf
facts.sourceTitle: Tree Management Permit Application (City of Colwood, 2017)
facts.excerpt: If you are cutting more than five protected trees, you will need to provide a Tree Management Plan prepared by a qualified professional.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. 2017 document; current online application may differ.

facts.text: Colwood's hillside and natural-hazard guidelines say to avoid development on slopes over 30%, discourage tree removal on steep slopes, and ask for exposed soil to be replanted with native Coastal Douglas-fir zone plants.
facts.excerpt: Development on slopes over 30% must be avoided
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Some OCP excerpts are from draft text; confirm against consolidated OCP Bylaw No. 1700.

facts.text: Colwood's riparian and marine-shoreline development permit area covers shoreline land up to 11 m above sea level, does not support shoreline hardening, and keeps structures out of the 100 m Esquimalt Lagoon sanctuary buffer.
facts.sourceTitle: 20. Riparian Areas and Marine Shorelines Environmental DPA (Colwood OCP)
facts.excerpt: Riparian Areas and Marine Shorelines Environmental DPA
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. The PDF is labelled DRAFT and a 2023 amendment proposed splitting it; confirm what is in force. Excerpt is the section title.

facts.text: Colwood's drier sites are Garry oak country; those ecosystems hold a high share of the region's rare species and fall under its Sensitive Ecosystems guidelines.
facts.excerpt: Garry oak ecosystems dominate other drier areas of Colwood
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing

facts.text: Open burning is not allowed in Colwood at any time, so yard debris is hauled rather than burned; certified outdoor wood appliances (firebox no larger than 24 by 24 in) are allowed except when the fire rating is high or extreme.
facts.excerpt: Outdoor wood burning appliances are permitted EXCEPT when the fire rating is HIGH or EXTREME
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Outdoor Burning Restriction and Regulation Bylaw No. 931.

facts.text: Royal Bay was a gravel operation from 1910 to 2009, and the City says the neighbourhood is still being reclaimed under a provincial Mine Reclamation Plan, so new yards there are often built on reworked sand and gravel.
facts.excerpt: continues to be reclaimed, repaired and restored as per the Mine Reclamation Plan
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. The 'reworked sand and gravel' soil inference is not stated by the City; soften or verify on site.

facts.text: Esquimalt Lagoon became a federal Migratory Bird Sanctuary in 1931, and the sanctuary includes about 100 m of the land around it, so waterfront yards near the lagoon sit beside protected habitat.
facts.sourceTitle: Esquimalt Lagoon Migratory Bird Sanctuary - Government of Canada
facts.excerpt: the lagoon and surrounding 100m of land
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Which source gave the 1931 date and the 100 m wording was unclear in the snippet; confirm on the federal page.

facts.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host not in allowed network); confirm wording on the page before publishing. Dates and day split also shown in the Saanich watering-schedules page snippet. Shared regional block, not municipality-specific.
